records.title: Vermont takes its dispatch and records platform offline

history.text: The FAA reported instability around 3:30 p.m. Eastern and ordered a nationwide ground stop.

Air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. Eastern on Nov 13.
El País reported that FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the agencies involved had concluded the failure was not a cyberattack. The FAA’s next-day written assessment used more qualified wording.
The FAA published its initial technical findings and said it had no indication of an attack.
The FAA temporarily paused related router installations.
Duffy said investigators still did not know why a router failure could disrupt so much of the network.

records.impactNote: The FAA halted departures nationwide. Flights already in the air could land.
records.assessment: The FAA reported no indication of an attack. The root cause remains open.

records.title: Actions, Pages, Copilot and webhooks disrupted
records.summary: GitHub reported problems across four products. The backlog of automation jobs cleared within the hour.

records.assessment: GitHub reported a service outage with no cyber attribution.

records.title: Mail, Photos and sign-in outage
records.summary: Some users lost iCloud Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Photos, and account sign-in. Find My had a separate, longer degradation during the same window.
records.rationale: Apple’s status page recorded the service impact. Coverage identified no public attribution to a cyberattack.

records.assessment: Apple acknowledged the outage and gave no security assessment.

records.title: Hockey federation takes its website offline
records.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation took its site offline after a pro-Russia message appeared on the homepage.
records.rationale: The federation publicly confirmed a cyberattack. The content of the message does not establish who posted it.

records.quote: The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has been the target of a cyberattack.

records.title: Hospital network failure postpones operations
records.summary: A network failure disrupted phones and IT services at the Brussels university hospital. Planned operations were postponed.
records.rationale: The hospital initially reported no indication of an attack. Its next-day statement ruled one out and said it had detected no data leak.
records.cause: Network failure. The hospital declined to identify the component that failed.
records.speaker: UZ Brussel · Dutch-language statement
records.quote: Er is geen sprake van een cyberaanval en er werd geen datalek vastgesteld.

history.text: The hospital postponed planned operations after the network failed.

records.impactNote: The hospital’s phones and IT systems were disrupted. Operations were postponed and partner hospitals also restored systems.
records.assessment: The hospital explicitly ruled out a cyberattack.

denial.speaker: UZ Brussel

records.title: University restricts access to campus systems
records.summary: Vanderbilt University restricted access to campus systems and initially told students and staff to shut down devices. The university said full recovery could take weeks.
records.rationale: The university identified an ongoing cyberattack and coordinated its response with law enforcement. A group’s claim of responsibility is a separate, unverified assertion.
records.cause: Cyberattack. The university did not attribute it to a particular group in its incident updates.
records.speaker: Vanderbilt University
records.quote: Vanderbilt University is coordinating our response to this ongoing cyberattack with government agencies, law enforcement and external cybersecurity partners.

history.text: The university announced the incident and restricted access to campus systems.
The university restored some services and said full recovery could take weeks.
Vanderbilt said the global Microsoft outage was separate from the attack on its campus systems.
Most campus applications were back online, including Oracle and Salesforce. OneDrive, SharePoint and Box remained disabled.

records.impactNote: Campus devices and university systems were affected. Classes continued while teams restored access.
records.assessment: Vanderbilt confirmed an ongoing cyberattack.
